newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bonds gained ground on Friday afternoon, well supported by positive U.S. jobs data and good expectations for Saturday's G7 meeting.
Despite lacklustre trade today, dealers in Madrid said bonos could climb in the coming week. January CPI is expected to show a fall in the year on year rate versus December's data.
"Today we had an almost dead market, until US job data showed a good number which awoke bond dealers all around the world," a trader said.
In January a robust 271,000 gain in U.S. employment, coupled with mild earnings growth, were seen as the best of both worlds.

Tomorrow's G7 meeting of finance ministers and central bankers in Berlin is expected to ratify recent dollar strength, an approach which could support peripheral markets and therefore bonos, dealers added.
Dealers shrugged off comments on monetary union from Kohl and Prodi, which were thought to add little.
But the Spanish market was positioning itself for a further jump, dealers said. January CPI data, due on February 13, is expected to improve to around 3.0 percent.
"We'll see a steepening in the yield curve," a dealer said.
The spread between two- and 10-year bonds, which rose to 127 basis points yesterday, ended almost unchanged at 126 bps.
But dealers pointed out that five-year bonds were among the best buys. The 7.9 percent February 2002 was trading at around 108.17/27, yielding around 5.91 percent.
